en liste.explanation: "En liste" means "a list". A common word built with it is "en gæsteliste" (a guest list). To say someone is on that list, say: "Du står på gæstelisten" (You are on the guest list).

en liter.explanation: "En liter" means "a liter". To name the liquid you measure, put it right after: "en liter vand" (a liter of water).

en litteraturliste.explanation: "En litteraturliste" means "a bibliography". It is built from "en litteratur" (literature) and "en liste" (a list).

en livredder.explanation: "En livredder" means "a lifeguard". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en redder" (a rescuer). To warn that something is deadly, use "liv" in another word: "Det er livsfarligt" (It is life-threatening).

en livret.explanation: "En livret" means "a favorite dish". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en ret" (a dish). To say how many dishes a dinner has, use "ret" in the plural: "en middag med tre retter" (a dinner with three dishes).

en livsstil.explanation: "En livsstil" means "a lifestyle". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en stil" (a style). To say something does not suit your taste, use the word "stil" alone: "Det er ikke min stil" (That is not my style).

en livstid.explanation: "En livstid" means "a lifetime". To say a judge sent someone to prison for life, use the same word: "Han fik livstid" (He got a life sentence).

en lobby.explanation: "En lobby" means "a lobby". English speakers would write "lobbies" for more than one, but the Danish plural is "lobbyer": "to lobbyer" (two lobbies).

en lobbyist.explanation: "En lobbyist" means "a lobbyist". The work such a person does is called "lobbyisme" (lobbying).

en loftslampe.explanation: "En loftslampe" means "a ceiling light". It is built from "et loft" (a ceiling) and "en lampe" (a lamp). To say where old things are stored, use "loft" for the attic: "Vi har gamle ting på loftet" (We have old things in the attic).

en lokalavis.explanation: "En lokalavis" means "a local newspaper". It is built from "lokal" (local) and "en avis" (a newspaper).

en lokalbefolkning.explanation: "En lokalbefolkning" means "a local population". It is built from "lokal" (local) and "en befolkning" (a population).

en lokomotivfører.explanation: "En lokomotivfører" means "a train driver". It is built from "et lokomotiv" (a locomotive) and "en fører" (a driver).

en lomme.explanation: "En lomme" means "a pocket". To say where you keep something, say: "Mine nøgler er i lommen" (My keys are in my pocket).

en lommelygte.explanation: "En lommelygte" means "a flashlight". It is built from "en lomme" (a pocket) and "en lygte" (a light). The part "lygte" is also in "en baglygte" (a taillight) and "en forlygte" (a headlight).

en lommeregner.explanation: "En lommeregner" means "a calculator". It is built from "en lomme" (a pocket) and "at regne" (to calculate). The part "lomme" is also in "lommepenge" (pocket money) and "en lommekniv" (a pocket knife).

en loppe.explanation: "En loppe" means "a flea". The start of the word is in "et loppemarked" (a flea market). To say you are going to one, say: "Vi går på loppemarked i morgen" (We are going to a flea market tomorrow).

en lov.explanation: "En lov" means "a law". To say something breaks the law, say: "Det er imod loven" (It is against the law). When you say something is allowed, "lov" also has that meaning: "Det er ikke lov at parkere her" (It is not allowed to park here).

en lufthavn.explanation: "En lufthavn" means "an airport". It is built from "luft" (air) and "en havn" (a harbor). To say where a boat is, use the word "havn" alone: "Båden ligger i havnen" (The boat is in the harbor).

en lugt.explanation: "En lugt" means "a smell". To describe a pleasant smell, use "en duft" (a scent): "Der er en duft af kaffe" (There is a scent of coffee).

en lukkedag.explanation: "En lukkedag" means "a closing day". It is built from "at lukke" (to close) and "en dag" (a day). To ask when a shop shuts for the day, use "en lukketid" (a closing time): "Hvad er lukketiden?" (What is the closing time?)

en lukketid.explanation: "En lukketid" means "a closing time". It is built from "at lukke" (to close) and "en tid" (a time). To say a place is shut for a whole day, use "en lukkedag" (a closing day): "Vi har lukkedag i morgen" (We are closed all day tomorrow).

en lunge.explanation: "En lunge" means "a lung". To name the illness, use "lungebetændelse" (pneumonia), built from "lunge" and "en betændelse" (an inflammation): "Hun har lungebetændelse" (She has pneumonia).

en lup.explanation: "En lup" means "a magnifying glass". To ask to borrow one, say: "Må jeg låne din lup?" (May I borrow your magnifying glass?)

en lur.explanation: "En lur" means "a nap". When you talk about a phone receiver, "lur" has that second meaning: "Han tog luren" (He picked up the receiver).

en lus.explanation: "En lus" means "a louse". The plural has no ending, so it looks the same as the singular: "to lus" (two lice).

en lyd.explanation: "En lyd" means "a sound". To tell someone to make a device louder, use the second meaning, the volume: "Skru op for lyden" (Turn up the volume).

en lydbog.explanation: "En lydbog" means "an audiobook". It is built from "en lyd" (a sound) and "en bog" (a book). English speakers would guess "lydbøger" wrongly as "lydbogs": the plural changes "o" to "ø", so two audiobooks are "to lydbøger".

en lygte.explanation: "En lygte" means "a light". To name a light for a bike, add "cykel" in front: "en cykellygte" (a bike light). To talk about a lamp in a room, use "en lampe" (a lamp): "Lampen står på bordet" (The lamp is on the table).

en lynlås.explanation: "En lynlås" means "a zipper". To say you close the zipper, say: "Jeg lukker lynlåsen" (I close the zipper).

en lysestage.explanation: "En lysestage" means "a candlestick". The first part, "lys", means "a candle" here. To say you light a candle, say: "Jeg tænder et lys" (I light a candle).

en lyskontakt.explanation: "En lyskontakt" means "a light switch". It is built from "lys" (light) and "en kontakt" (a switch). To ask someone to turn the light on, say: "Tænd lyset" (Turn on the light).

en lysning.explanation: "En lysning" means "a clearing". It comes from "lys" (light). To say where a clearing is, add "i skoven" (in the forest): "en lysning i skoven" (a clearing in the forest).

en lyspære.explanation: "En lyspære" means "a lightbulb". It is built from "lys" (light) and "en pære" (a pear). To say you replace a burned-out bulb, say: "Jeg skifter pæren" (I change the bulb).

en lytteøvelse.explanation: "En lytteøvelse" means "a listening exercise". It is built from "at lytte" (to listen) and "en øvelse" (an exercise). "At lytte" means to listen on purpose: "Jeg lytter til musik" (I listen to music). "At høre" means to hear without trying: "Jeg hører en lyd" (I hear a sound).

en låge.explanation: "En låge" means "a gate". To talk about a large gate for cars, use "en port" (a large gate): "Bilen holder foran porten" (The car stops in front of the gate).

en lås.explanation: "En lås" means "a lock". The matching verb is "at låse" (to lock): "Husk at låse døren" (Remember to lock the door).

en læbe.explanation: "En læbe" means "a lip". To name the makeup for your lips, use "en læbestift" (a lipstick): "Hun køber en læbestift" (She buys a lipstick).

en læbestift.explanation: "En læbestift" means "a lipstick". It starts with "en læbe" (a lip), which is also in "en læbepomade" (a lip balm).

en læg.explanation: "En læg" means "a calf (of the leg)". Do not mix it up with "en læge" (a doctor), which has one more letter: "Jeg ringer til lægen" (I call the doctor).

en læge.explanation: "En læge" means "a doctor". To say you are going to see your doctor, say: "Jeg går til lægen" (I am going to the doctor).

en lægevagt.explanation: "En lægevagt" means "an after-hours medical service". It is built from "en læge" (a doctor) and "en vagt" (a duty).

en lænestol.explanation: "En lænestol" means "an armchair". It is built from "at læne sig" (to lean back) and "en stol" (a chair).

en længde.explanation: "En længde" means "a length". To say how many times you swim from one end of a pool to the other, use the same word: "Jeg svømmer ti længder" (I swim ten lengths).

en lænke.explanation: "En lænke" means "a chain". To say a prisoner was chained, say: "Fangen blev lagt i lænker" (The prisoner was put in chains). For an ordinary chain, such as on a bike, use "en kæde" (a chain): "Cyklen har en rusten kæde" (The bike has a rusty chain).

en lærebog.explanation: "En lærebog" means "a textbook". It is built from "at lære" (to learn) and "en bog" (a book). "At lære" also means "to teach": "Hun lærer mig dansk" (She teaches me Danish).

en lærer.explanation: "En lærer" means "a teacher", for a man or a woman. To say someone's job, leave out "en": "Hun er lærer" (She is a teacher).

en lærestreg.explanation: "En lærestreg" means "a hard lesson". To talk about a lesson in school, use "en lektion" (a lesson): "Lektionen starter klokken ni" (The lesson starts at nine o'clock).

en lærling.explanation: "En lærling" means "an apprentice". In Denmark, an apprentice learns a trade by working at a company and also by attending trade school.

en læser.explanation: "En læser" means "a reader". The same word is also the verb form of "at læse" (to read): "Hun læser en bog" (She reads a book).

en læsesal.explanation: "En læsesal" means "a reading room". It is built from "at læse" (to read) and "en sal" (a hall).

en læsning.explanation: "En læsning" means "a reading". To say you give your own understanding of a text, use it with "en": "en kritisk læsning af romanen" (a critical reading of the novel). To talk about reading as a skill or school subject, leave out "en": "Vi har læsning i anden time" (We have reading in second period).

en løbesko.explanation: "En løbesko" means "a running shoe". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "en sko" (a shoe). The plural has no ending: "to løbesko" (two running shoes). The start "løbe-" means "for running" in other words too: "et løbebånd" (a treadmill).

en løbetur.explanation: "En løbetur" means "a run". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "en tur" (a trip). To say it is someone's turn, "tur" has another meaning: "Det er din tur" (It is your turn).

en løgn.explanation: "En løgn" means "a lie". To say someone told a lie, use "at fortælle" (to tell) with it: "Han fortalte en løgn" (He told a lie).

en løgner.explanation: "En løgner" means "a liar". It is a blunt word, and calling someone "en løgner" is a strong accusation. To say in a milder way that a statement is wrong, say: "Det passer ikke" (That is not true).

en løjtnant.explanation: "En løjtnant" means "a lieutenant". English speakers would spell it like the English word, but the Danish spelling is "løjtnant", with "ø" and "j" at the start.

en løkke.explanation: "En løkke" means "a loop". To talk about computer code that repeats the same steps, use the same word: "en løkke i programmet" (a loop in the program).

en løn.explanation: "En løn" means "a salary". To talk about pay for each hour, use "timeløn" (hourly pay).

en lønforhøjelse.explanation: "En lønforhøjelse" means "a raise". It is built from "løn" (pay) and "en forhøjelse" (an increase). To say what you would like from your boss, say: "Jeg vil gerne have en lønforhøjelse" (I would like a raise).

en lønseddel.explanation: "En lønseddel" means "a paystub". The part "seddel" (a slip of paper) is also in "en pengeseddel" (a banknote). Note the spelling of "the paystub": "lønsedlen" has one "d" less than "lønseddel".

en løsning.explanation: "En løsning" means "a solution". It comes from "at løse" (to solve). To say you find a way out of a problem, say: "Vi finder en løsning" (We find a solution).

en løve.explanation: "En løve" means "a lion". To say a female lion, use "en løvinde" (a lioness): "Løvinden ligger i skyggen" (The lioness lies in the shade). The word is also the first part of "en løvetand" (a dandelion), literally "lion tooth".

et laboratorium.explanation: "Et laboratorium" means "a laboratory". The plural drops "um" and ends in "-er": "to laboratorier" (two laboratories).

et lag.explanation: "Et lag" means "a layer". The word is also the start of "en lagkage" (a layer cake): "Vi spiser lagkage" (We eat layer cake).

et lagen.explanation: "Et lagen" means "a sheet", as in a bed sheet. To ask for a sheet of paper, use "et ark" (a sheet of paper): "Giv mig et ark papir" (Give me a sheet of paper).

et lager.explanation: "Et lager" means "a warehouse / stock". To ask whether a shop has an item, say: "Er den på lager?" (Is it in stock?)

et lam.explanation: "Et lam" means "a lamb". To talk about lamb as meat, leave out "et": "Jeg elsker lam" (I love lamb).

et land.explanation: "Et land" means "a country". The same word also means "countryside" in "på landet" (in the countryside). To say where you live, say: "Jeg bor på landet" (I live in the countryside).

et landbrug.explanation: "Et landbrug" means "agriculture / a farm". To talk about farming as an industry, say: "Der er meget landbrug i Danmark" (There is a lot of agriculture in Denmark). To talk about the farmhouse and its yard, use "en gård" (a farm): "Vi bor på en gård" (We live on a farm).

et landkort.explanation: "Et landkort" means "a map". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "et kort" (a map or a card). The plural has no ending: "to landkort" (two maps).

et landshold.explanation: "Et landshold" means "a national team". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "et hold" (a team). To say a player is on that team, say: "Han spiller på landsholdet" (He plays on the national team).

et landskab.explanation: "Et landskab" means "a landscape". To talk about what you see from one spot, use "en udsigt" (a view): "Der er en flot udsigt fra bjerget" (There is a nice view from the mountain).

et lavtryk.explanation: "Et lavtryk" means "a low-pressure system". It is built from "lav" (low) and "et tryk" (pressure). The opposite is "et højtryk" (a high-pressure system): "Et højtryk ligger over Danmark" (A high-pressure system lies over Denmark).

et led.explanation: "Et led" means "a joint". To say something is one step in a series, use "et led i kæden" (a link in the chain).

et leksikon.explanation: "Et leksikon" means "an encyclopedia". To look up the meaning of a word instead, use "en ordbog" (a dictionary): "Jeg slår ordet op i en ordbog" (I look the word up in a dictionary).

et lig.explanation: "Et lig" means "a corpse". It is a blunt word. A gentler way to speak of a dead person is "den afdøde" (the deceased person): "Familien sørger over den afdøde" (The family mourns the deceased person).

et like.explanation: "Et like" means "a like". To say you give one on social media, say: "Jeg giver et like" (I give a like).

et link.explanation: "Et link" means "a link". To ask someone to send one, say: "Send mig et link" (Send me a link).

et liv.explanation: "Et liv" means "a life". To talk about life in general, use the form "livet": "Livet er godt" (Life is good). To talk about one person's life, use "et liv": "at have et godt liv" (to have a good life).

et loft.explanation: "Et loft" means "a ceiling / attic". When you talk about the top of a room, it means "ceiling": "Der er en lampe i loftet" (There is a lamp in the ceiling). When you talk about the space under the roof, it means "attic": "Vi har gamle ting på loftet" (We have old things in the attic).

et loftsrum.explanation: "Et loftsrum" means "an attic room". It is built from "et loft" (an attic) and "et rum" (a room).

related.en: a top floor under the roof

et loppemarked.explanation: "Et loppemarked" means "a flea market". It is built from "en loppe" (a flea) and "et marked" (a market). To say you go to one, say: "Vi går på loppemarked i morgen" (We are going to a flea market tomorrow).

et lotteri.explanation: "Et lotteri" means "a lottery". To say someone won a prize in one, say: "Han vandt i lotteriet" (He won the lottery). The plural is "lotterier": "to lotterier" (two lotteries).

et lovforslag.explanation: "Et lovforslag" means "a bill". It is built from "lov" (law) and "et forslag" (a proposal). To say parliament approves one, use "at vedtage" (to pass): "Folketinget vedtager lovforslaget" (The Danish parliament passes the bill).

et lykønskningskort.explanation: "Et lykønskningskort" means "a congratulations card". It is built from "en lykønskning" (a congratulation) and "et kort" (a card). To congratulate someone aloud, say: "Tillykke!" (Congratulations!)

et lyskryds.explanation: "Et lyskryds" means "an intersection with traffic lights". It is built from "lys" (light) and "et kryds" (a cross). For an intersection without traffic lights, use "et vejkryds" (an intersection): "Vi mødes i vejkrydset" (We meet at the intersection).

et lån.explanation: "Et lån" means "a loan". The verb "at låne" means both "to borrow" and "to lend": "Jeg låner dig en pen" (I lend you a pen).

et lår.explanation: "Et lår" means "a thigh". To name a part of a chicken, put the animal in front: "et kyllingelår" (a chicken thigh).

et læserbrev.explanation: "Et læserbrev" means "a letter to the editor". It is built from "en læser" (a reader) and "et brev" (a letter). English speakers would guess the plural wrongly: it is "læserbreve", not "læserbrever".

et løbebånd.explanation: "Et løbebånd" means "a treadmill". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "et bånd" (a belt). The plural has no ending: "to løbebånd" (two treadmills).

et løfte.explanation: "Et løfte" means "a promise". To say you keep a promise, use "at holde" (to hold): "Jeg holder mit løfte" (I keep my promise). To say you break one, use "at bryde" (to break): "Han brød sit løfte" (He broke his promise).

et løg.explanation: "Et løg" means "an onion". The word is also part of "hvidløg" (garlic), literally "white onion".

lad os se.explanation: "Lad os se" means "Let's see." To suggest doing something together, put "lad os" (let us) before a verb: "Lad os gå" (Let us go). To say you will check, answer a question like this: "Er der mere mælk?" "Lad os se." (Is there more milk? Let's see.)

lad være.explanation: "Lad være" means "Don't!" To tell someone not to do something, add "med at" and a verb: "Lad være med at ringe" (Don't call). In the past, "lad" becomes "lod": "Han lod være" (He left it alone).

lakrids.explanation: "Lakrids" means "licorice". To name ice cream with that flavor, add "is" (ice cream): "lakridsis" (licorice ice cream).

laks.explanation: "Laks" means "salmon". To count whole fish, use "en laks" (a salmon): "Han fanger en laks" (He catches a salmon). To talk about salmon as food, leave out "en": "Jeg spiser laks" (I eat salmon).

laktosefri.explanation: "Laktosefri" means "lactose-free". It is built from "laktose" (lactose) and "fri" (free). The same ending is in "glutenfri" (gluten-free) and "sukkerfri" (sugar-free). With a word that takes "et", add "t": "et laktosefrit produkt" (a lactose-free product).

lammekød.explanation: "Lammekød" means "lamb", the meat. It is built from "et lam" (a lamb) and "kød" (meat).

lammet.explanation: "Lammet" means "paralyzed". To say someone is frozen by fear, use it too: "Hun stod lammet af skræk" (She stood paralyzed by fear). Do not mix it up with "lammet" meaning "the lamb", which is "et lam" (a lamb) with "the" added: "Lammet løber" (The lamb runs).
